target_customer: App developers who need data sync (platform), plus consumers using Simplenote as the showcase notes app
problem: Developers had to build their own cross-device data sync; Simplenote showed the need for simple note sync that Apple's Notes lacked at the time.
business_model: developer sync platform with a free consumer notes app as showcase
product_category: data sync platform and notes app

founders.name: Fred Cheng
founders.background_notes: Only founder listed on the YC page; no background given there.

founders.name: Mike Johnston
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by TechCrunch in January 2013; not listed on the YC page. Background not found.

competitors.name: Apple Notes
competitors.what: built-in iPhone notes app that synced over USB and lacked search in 2010

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable multi-device sync with conflict handling was hard for a team of two to three, run on Google App Engine, but the problem was well understood.

defensibility.rationale: Users held notes in the service, but note apps and sync backends were abundant and Simplenote was a simple app.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Neither copied it directly; Automattic bought Simperium in January 2013 and relaunched Simplenote in 2013.

market_need_then: Shawn Blanc's August 2010 review credited Simplenote with over the air sync and better typography as big improvements over Apple Notes, which synced over USB.

branding.domain_note: A secondary summary of TechCrunch says Matt Mullenweg helped buy the Simplenote.com domain; unverified.
branding.community_and_virality: Third party Mac and Windows note tools synced with Simplenote, per search coverage.

brand_strength.rationale: Simplenote was well regarded by reviewers but sources show no brand work, and Simperium the company name was little known.

outcome_analysis: Simperium raised only 450 thousand dollars in 2011, built a sync platform that powered the well liked Simplenote app, and reached about 750 thousand registered users before Automattic acquired it in January 2013. The product lives on in Automattic's portfolio, though one unverified source says active development has stopped, so the exit looks like a small but real success.
notes: simperium.com is alive and shows an Automattic footer. The 450 thousand seed amount appears in TechCrunch and in an aggregator; CB Insights lists a different investor (Frictionless Ventures) and no amount. Acquisition price not disclosed. Founder education and employers not found. Simplenote was first built in 2008, before the YC batch. Evernote was described as the comparison by TechCrunch in 2013 only, so it is not in the founding competitor list.
